questions.question: should I treat my boots out of box ? Annnnd how often should I treat them ?

hybrid.answer:
**Short version:** it depends on the boot. For finished, pretreated leather he relays the brand's advice not to treat out of the box. For distressed or rustic leather he recommends treating it. As for how often, his latest word (2022) is to do it when the boots look or feel dry, not on a fixed schedule.

**Out of the box**
- Reading Blundstone's FAQ, he says most of their boots come pretreated and the brand doesn't recommend treating them out of the box [1].
- Rustic Brown, Crazy Horse and rustic black leathers are the exception. They're made to look distressed and don't carry the same pretreatments as finished, oiled leather [2].
- For those, he says to treat them "100%" and not keep them dry, because untreated leather dries out and cracks [3].
- This is what he says about Blundstones specifically. He hasn't covered other boot brands in the videos available here.

**How often**
- **Most recent (2022):** he treats his boots when he feels they need it. He admits he probably does too little, and notes others are more regimented [4]. His test is simple: if the leather looks or feels dry, or water isn't beading on top, it needs more wax. If it looks dry, it needs oil [5].
- He also says to clean boots regularly, because dirt wears leather down faster [6].
- **Earlier (2019):** he was more specific, saying you may have to wax them every month, or even every week if you're really hard on them [7]. By 2022 he had moved away from a set schedule toward going by feel.

**Order, if you do treat them:** he says to clean first, then condition, then wax [8].

questions.question: So if I buy the levis 501 shrink to fit will they get tighter after washing?

hybrid.answer:
**Yes, the first soak or wash tightens them, mainly in the waist, but with wear they loosen again.** He recommends buying them bigger than your usual size for that reason.

**Most recent advice (2025):** he says you should usually go two sizes up in a shrink-to-fit 501 [1].

**How much they shrink (2023):** his shrunk 501 STFs came out smaller than regular rinsed 501s [2]. How you wash them matters. He says to skip very hot water and the dryer, because that is what gave him a really nice fit [3]. He thinks that with frequent wear they would stretch out to about the same size as the rinsed pair [4].

**His first pair (2019):** after the hot soak and air-dry, he says they definitely slimmed up, mostly in the waist [5]. The length barely changed [6]. The waist was very tight at first. A week later it had stretched enough to wear a belt [7].

**Sizing advice:**
- In 2021 he says Levi's advice is correct: size up two in the waist and two inches in length [8].
- In 2020 he bought a 29 waist and 30 length. He could barely pull them on and couldn't breathe, but a year later he calls the fit really good for him. He says he should have gotten a 32 length [9].

questions.question: I'm usually a 33x30 in Levi's 502s, what size should I buy in these? [501 STF]

hybrid.answer:
By his rule, you'd look for a **35 waist x 32 length** in the 501 STF: two sizes up in the waist and two inches more in length. He hasn't covered how the 502's fit compares with the 501, so this applies his rule to your usual size.

**His current advice (2025):** He says you should usually go two sizes up in the 501 STF [1]. In his 2021 LVC video he spells it out as two sizes up in the waist and "two inches more" in length, and says Levi's advice is correct [2]. In his 2023 Wrangler comparison, his size 32 STFs, bought two sizes up from a 30 rinsed pair, were the example [3].

**He used to ignore this.** In 2019 he skipped Levi's sizing advice and bought a 29x30 [4]. A year later he said the waist was too tight at first, but it fit well once the jeans loosened up. He also said he would definitely have gotten a 32 length [5]. By 2021 he was saying it took him four pairs of 501s to realize Levi's sizing advice is right [2].

**Caveat:** He jokes that if you wear a 34 you'd want a 36, "although I don't think a 36 exists" [2]. A 35 waist may not exist either, and he doesn't say whether to round up or down in that case.

questions.question: Why do you cuff your jeans?

hybrid.answer:
He cuffs mainly to manage length and to deal with wide legs. In his most recent video here (2020) he cuffed his Levi's 501s because he doesn't think his current style suits wider-legged pants left uncuffed. He also says he should have bought a 32 length, so the cuff partly covers jeans that came up short [1].

**Length (2019):** When trying on the unshrunk 501s, he says length is the first thing for him. If jeans look too long they just look bad, and the cuff shouldn't be too thick [2].

**Slimming wide legs:** He tried a basic cuff and a pin roll on the very wide 501s. Both made them look a little better, though still wider than he likes [3]. He also notes that pin-rolling his Gap jeans slims them more than normal [4].

**With boots, a shift:** In a late-2019 boots video he says he always used to cuff his jeans but now likes them worn down over his boots more. He thinks that calms the boots down as a loud fashion piece [5]. That is about boots specifically. In 2020 he still cuffed his 501s [1].

questions.question: So do you prefer [the Red Wing 3335s] over the 1907s?

hybrid.answer:
Yes in 2022, when he called the 3335s his favorite boots ever, but by September 2023 he hedged: the 3335s "still might be" his favorite Red Wings, "but they probably not," and he was selling them.

**Newest view (Sept 2023):** He says he is on record calling the 3335s his favorite Red Wings of all time. He adds that they still might be, but probably not. He says the 875s, the 1907s and the Iron Rangers each have characteristics he really likes [1]. He still credits the 3335s for being stitch-down, lighter, more nimble and easier for walking or a light hike, but they were on his list of boots to go [1].

**Earlier view (Oct 2022):** He said the 3335s were his favorite boots he'd ever had and that they beat his Blundstones, the 1907s and the 875s [2]. His reasons: he isn't doing heritage work but going on hikes and walking in the woods. He called the 1907s and 875s more beefily constructed, so you'd choose those if you need a tough boot, but he thought the 3335s were a dramatically better all-around boot [2]. He also said they look way cooler [3].

**Construction:** Even in 2022 he didn't think stitch-down gave the 3335s a big edge over Goodyear-welted boots. He said they aren't some infinitely better level than the 1907s or 875s, partly because they use a single stitch [4].

questions.question: How do you feel bout blunnies as of Late 2023?

hybrid.answer:
As of September 2023, he's still a big fan of Blundstones, but he's cutting down his collection and retiring his well-worn 585s. He says they're "just incredible" and that he's "always loved them," though he's let go of some pairs.

**His latest view (Sept 2023)**
- His 585s, the subject of his first video, have held up. He says they've stayed "probably my most water resistant boots through it all" and he's "a big fan of them," but he thinks "it's time to retire those bunnies." [1]
- He notes that some people seem not to like Blundstones. [1]
- He's also letting go of his heavy-duty Blundstone work boots. He thought they were waterproof, but they're only very water-resistant nubuck. [2] He describes them as steel-toe, fire and electrical hazard resistant boots that add about two inches to his height. [2]
- He keeps a slip-on pair, which he groups with other shoes he can "flop on really quick" for errands or rain. He says he's keeping them but "could easily put them on the sell list." [3]

**Where he started (2019)**
- In his first-impressions review he said he'd recommend them "100%" if you're going to treat them. [4] He warned that untreated leather isn't hydrophobic and can dry out and crack. [4]
- He called them "by far my favorites" of his three or four boots at the time. [5]

**Overall**
He's still positive on Blundstones. The 2023 sell-off is about making room, and his well-worn 585s are being retired after proving durable.

questions.question: How does the made in England boot stack up to Solovairs? [Dr. Martens]

hybrid.answer:
He favors Solovair over the Made in England Dr. Martens for most buyers, unless you specifically want the yellow stitching. His only direct comparison is in his 2022 Dr. Martens video, and his 2023 England-vs-Thailand video doesn't mention Solovair.

**Materials:** He says the Made in England leather "will age fine" and is probably on par with Solovair's, and the better midsoles are probably on par too [1]. The Made in England pair isn't clearly better on these points.

**Price:** He says Solovairs are cheaper than the Made in England Docs [2]. He says the England versions cost about a third more, and that you're mostly paying for the "made in England" part [3].

**Comfort and repair:** Solovairs have a shank, which he says makes them a bit more comfortable over long periods [4]. He also says they're welted in a more accepted way, so they're easier to resole [5]. Docs are easier to break in from the start, but Solovairs are tougher at first and give more comfort down the line [6].

**Same boot:** He says the derby eight-eyed Solovair is essentially the exact same boot as Doc Martens, from the original maker. The only thing it lacks is the yellow stitching. If the stitching matters to you, he says you'd have to get the Made in England Docs [7][8].

**Caveat:** He loves Solovair but had problems with his own pair. After eight wears, a tab on the back had ripped off and a lace had snapped. He assumed it was a manufacturing defect and expected the company to fix it [9].

**2023 follow-up:** In his later video he judges the Made in England 1460 against the Thailand 1460, not against Solovair. He says it's probably not worth the extra $90 on a purely practical basis [10]. He adds that you have to be a mega fan to get it [11].

questions.question: Hi, I am going on a 4 day hike and I am wondering if I can use my blundstone for them, what do you think?

hybrid.answer:
He hasn't covered multi-day hikes in the videos available here, but his closest comments suggest caution: he has hiked in his Blundstones, though he says they aren't good boots for mountaining because of weak ankle support.

**Most relevant (2020, one-year review):** He took his Blundstone 585s up and down mountains in Maine, and they got scuffed but "held up well" [1]. He also says they "are not good boots for mountaining apparently because they don't have uh good ankle support" [2]. On a 4-day hike, that ankle support is the main thing to think about.

**Later view (2023):** He says his heavily worn 585s "have held up through it all" and are "probably my most water resistant boots" [3]. That is about durability and water resistance, not hiking comfort over several days.

**Care (2019):** He recommends the boots only if you'll keep them treated. He says to "buy these boots knowing that you'll have to take care of them" [4]. If yours are the rustic distressed style, that matters for wet trail conditions. On first impressions he reported walking around a city and through the woods with no blisters [5].

**What he hasn't said:** He hasn't tested Blundstones over several consecutive days of hiking, with a loaded pack, or on rough terrain. For a purpose-built hiking boot, the closest thing he mentions is the Hoka Kaha 2 GTX, which he describes as feeling like "a perfectly molded spaceship that locks your feet in" [6]. He says he's keeping them for a hiking comparison, and that video isn't covered here.

**Bottom line from his comments:** Fine for casual hikes by his account, but ankle support is his stated weak point, and a 4-day trip goes beyond anything he tested.

questions.question: I'm 5'11-225 lbs with a dad bod. What's the most cost efficient and quality t shirt for me? Also, what size would u prefer?

hybrid.answer:
He doesn't give a size for your build, but his rule for bigger guys is to skip Uniqlo and go with Muji. At 5'11" and 225 lbs that makes **Muji** the best value pick, with **Front General Store** or **House of Blanks** as the step up.

**Best value for a bigger guy: Muji**
- He calls the $20 Uniqlo "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [1].
- He adds that if you're "taller or wider in any way, shape, or form, you'd want Muji" [2]. It costs about $4-5 more but is significantly longer and a good deal wider, and he says you'd probably like it if you're a little bigger [2].
- In June 2025 he said Muji feels justified at about $10 more than Uniqlo, with a thicker, tighter collar and a nicer feel [3].

**If you'll spend a bit more**
- Front General Store is his pick for the day in his September 2025 video: "Today I'm feeling the Front General Store" [4]. It's a $40 shirt made 100% in Japan, with "great proportions, great feel" [2].
- House of Blanks is $35, made in Canada, with zero torque, and he calls it "truly an outstanding value" [5]. He says to pick it if you want it perfectly smooth, and Front General Store if you want more character [4].
- In June 2025 he also said Bronson ($29) and Bravestar ($32) are neck and neck on value, though he'd give Bronson's standard loopwheel tubular tee the win over Bravestar [6].

**Size**
- He hasn't said what size he'd pick for 5'11" and 225 lbs.
- His own taste is a lot of room across the shoulders [7].
- On Los Angeles Apparel he said that if you size down one it might win [8].
- His one firm size rule is to size up one in Samurai [9].
- Muji's extra width and length are his answer for bigger builds, so go by each brand's measurements rather than a single size.

questions.question: Where's Whitesville?? It's literally the most well known White Tee from Japan

hybrid.answer:
Whitesville is in the video, in the vintage-style section. He recommends it, though he doesn't call it the most well-known Japanese white tee. He describes it as coming from a Japanese company riffing on old Americana underwear.[1]

**His take on Whitesville**
- He calls it "the jacked Instagram model special" and says it's cut like vintage t-shirts, which were underwear. That means it's very tight.[1]
- His verdict: "all in all I'd really recommend it."[2]
- He says it's "by far one of the softest t-shirts on the list."[3]
- The collar is what convinces him it's worth the price. It has binding tape over the collar, so it holds its shape better over time.[4]
- Shrink test: 5.4% in width and 3% in length.[5]

**Versus Velva Sheen**
He calls the two the same idea with very different execution. Whitesville feels soft, fluffy and plush, with slightly longer sleeves.[6] He says Velva Sheen is the more authentic of the two, because Whitesville is technically referencing it.[7]

**Not covered here**
His final superlatives and overall winner aren't available here, so I can't say whether Whitesville won any award.

questions.question: Am I the only one who loves these videos but in the end still has no idea which to buy? Please just tell me: buy this one, or these 3. I can't decide between 25 options. [t-shirts]

hybrid.answer:
You're not the only one, and he says as much: in his September 2025 roundup he stresses that there's no single best tee, because it comes down to your preferences [1]. Still, going by what he actually picks, here's a simple version.

**If you buy just one: Uniqlo ($20).** He says it's "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" and calls it a starter tee [2]. If you're taller or wider, he says to get Muji instead [3].

**If you buy three, he points to these:**
- **Uniqlo**, as above, for the cheap everyday option [2].
- **Front General Store** ($40, made in Japan), his value pick on the day he recorded. He says he's feeling it "today" and might feel House of Blanks "tomorrow", so it's not a hard rule [4]. Pick Front General Store if you want character and feel [4]. If you'd rather have perfectly smooth, no-torque, he says go House of Blanks ($35) [4].
- **J. Press x American Trench**, his pick among the all-arounders. He prefers its rougher hand feel and more structure [5].

**Other picks, depending on what you want:**
- **Wonder Looper**, his Japan's-might winner for its more universal fit [6].
- **Merz b. Schwanen 2M15**, his Supremes pick [7].
- **American Giant Everest**, his heavyweight winner, though he says it's far too heavy for most people [8].
- **Bronson**, which he says usually wins or comes close in other people's comparisons [9]. In June 2025 he called its $29 tee a very good shirt, but it's not actually loopwheel [10].

He hasn't named one overall winner for every body type or taste. This is how his preferences stack up.

questions.question: 1907 vs the 875's? What's the difference?

hybrid.answer:
In his view, the 1907 is the better buy of the two. He calls it Red Wing's best heritage boot and says to get it if you're looking at a Red Wing moc toe [1]. The main differences are the welt, the footbed and the laces, for about $10 more.

**Welt construction**
- The 875 is Goodyear welted. He calls Goodyear welts durable and pretty water resistant, with space for a cork footbed [2].
- The 1907 has a storm (Norwegian-style) welt, which he finds invaluable [3].
- He notes the popular view that Red Wing's version is just another leather strip stitched onto the welt, and he says he isn't quite sure [4].

**Price and extras**
- The 1907 costs about $10 more than the 875 [5].
- For that, it includes a removable leather footbed, which he says typically sells separately for $40, and leather laces, typically $15 [3].
- He also likes that the footbeds can be pulled out at the end of the day so the boots dry faster [3].

**Soles**
- He says he doesn't really like the crepe soles on the 1907 [1].
- He also says the 875 has crepe soles that he thinks will break down faster than the 3335's Vibram sole, so this isn't a difference between the two [6].

**Water resistance**
- He tested only the 1907. The right boot leaked almost immediately through the stitching and the left stayed dry [7].
- He still says he has no doubt they would hold up fine in rain, grass or mud [7].

**Later context**
By 2022 his favorite Red Wings were the stitch-down 3335s, which he says beat both the 1907 and the 875. He describes the 1907 and 875 as the beefier boots if you need something tough [8]. In 2023 he says the 875, the 1907 and the Iron Rangers each have characteristics he really likes [9]. He hasn't said that changes his 2021 pick of the 1907 as the best moc toe.

questions.question: How does Uniqlo compare to The Front General Store,  Proclub, and Hanes? ie what is the best budget shirt?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** In his most recent take (Sept 2025), Uniqlo is the best budget t-shirt. He calls the $20 Uniqlo "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [1]. He never ranks it head-to-head against Pro Club or Hanes, so those comparisons are only indirect.

**Uniqlo**
- He calls it "your starter t-shirt." It is open-ended and kind of rough, and he suggests Muji instead if you're taller or wider [2].
- In June 2025 he said that at $15 it's very good, with a bound neck collar that doesn't wiggle, and "You could end the video here" [4].
- In 2024 he recommended the heavyweight crew as a candidate for best bargain t-shirt [6]. Its shrink test was 2.3% in width and 2% in length [7].

**Front General Store**
- It's the step up in price. He describes it as a $40, 100% made-in-Japan shirt with great proportions and a great feel [3], and in June 2025 called it "still really good" [5].
- In 2024 he recommended it as an upgrade if you don't want to spend over $40, and gave it a softness score of 6 out of 10 [8].
- He said it came in second or tied for a previous win, though he sounded unsure of the details [3].

**Pro Club**
- He likes it, but says it is "the roughest shirt on this list" [9]. He gave it a softness score of 4 out of 10, with shrinkage of 2.78% in width and 6.86% in length [9].

**Hanes**
- He calls it "your classic $10 great shirt" and gave it a softness score of 7 out of 10 [10].

**Bottom line:** For the best value overall, he points to Uniqlo. Front General Store is the nicer, pricier option, while Hanes is the cheapest of the group at about $10 and Pro Club is the roughest. He hasn't put Hanes or Pro Club in a direct ranking against Uniqlo.

questions.question: Would you recommend this or the flint and tinder for someone who would use it like a rain jacket but also a windbreaker and a spring light jacket?

hybrid.answer:
He'd likely be comfortable recommending the Flint and Tinder for that mix, but it's unclear which jacket "this" refers to, so I can only say what he's said about the Flint and Tinder and a couple of lighter alternatives.

**Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker (2025, sponsored video)**
- He says it's for everyone, and that it's "not crazy lightweight, but it is a lighter weight, so it's comfortable." [1]
- It's cut well with full freedom of movement, and it's lined so you don't get wax on your skin. [1][2]
- He calls the $300 price the real magic for a lined, US-made waxed jacket in Martexin fabric, and says it's hard not to recommend. [2]
- Part of that video was a paid Huckberry read, but he says he'd talked about this jacket many times before being sponsored. [3]

**Rain use**
- In his 2023 comparison, he says the Huckberry waxed trucker suits a regular guy who likes to wear it when it's raining, with a hat. That video describes the Huckberry jacket as the lightest fabric of its group, unlined, and wearable when it's a little warmer. It doesn't say outright that this is the same jacket as the Flint and Tinder. [4][5]

**Lighter alternative: Barbour**
- If light and all-season matters most, he points to Barbour. It has his lightest fabric of the 2025 video (6 oz Sylkoil), and he says you can wear it in fall, summer or spring. [6]
- He also calls it "not a designated rain jacket," but it has storm cuffs and hood snaps. [6][7]

**Not covered**
He doesn't specifically rate the Flint and Tinder as a windbreaker, or compare it head-to-head on wind resistance.

questions.question: Great video. But just curious, how can you say it's a con that the Huckberry jacket is unlined when they sell two different versions of lined waxed truckers: wool, and flannel?

hybrid.answer:
In his 2025 video he describes the Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker as lined, so the unlined con from his 2023 video seems to be about the version he reviewed then. He calls it a personal-preference con, not a flaw in the jacket.

**2023 (the video you're asking about):** He called the Huckberry waxed trucker "the cheapest most simple unlined basic jacket on this list" [1]. He gave the con as: "the one con that Rogue territory and huckberry have for me is that they are not lined" [2]. His reason was that he "personally always like[s] aligning on wax jackets just so the wax isn't touching your clothes or your arms" [3].

**2025 (his latest word):** He says the Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker is "lined, so that way it's comfortable. You don't get wax on your skin" [4]. He also mentions "a really nice wool lined one that I'm yet to get" [4]. In both videos he calls the jacket Huckberry's number one selling product [5][6], so they appear to be the same jacket line. He doesn't say outright that it was changed. He also doesn't mention a flannel-lined version in the videos available here.

**His view on lining has softened too.** In the 2025 Rogue Territory section he says that although he usually wants a liner on wax jackets, "in my old age... I kind of see why you wouldn't line something" [7]. Satin-lined sleeves can limit how often you can wear the jacket and start to stick to your skin when it's warm [7].

questions.question: Do you know how these fit compared to the 875s? [Red Wing 3335s]

hybrid.answer:
He hasn't directly compared the fit of the 3335s to the 875s in the videos available here. He says the 3335s fit true to size but are slim and tapered, and can feel tight in the toes with wool socks.

**3335s:** He sized true to size and says they fit fine [1]. He adds that the profile is very slim and the boots taper down [1]. In warm weather with thin cotton socks he felt no discomfort or tightness. With wool socks on, his toes feel squished and he can't wiggle them much [1].

**875s:** He doesn't give 875 sizing. The closest he offers is for the Red Wing 1907, a Goodyear-welted moc toe like the 875. He usually wears an 8 in boots, bought an 8 in Red Wings, and they fit perfect [2]. His general rule for Red Wing leather boots is to buy them snug, not squished, because the leather is stiff at first and molds to your feet [2].

**Takeaway:** He doesn't say the 3335s fit differently from the 875s. What he does say is that the 3335s are slimmer and more tapered than you might expect, so if you plan to wear thick wool socks, that's where he found them tight.
